alignments.note: Temporal preposition before an infinitive construct takes 'When' (rule 52).
Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied 'the' into its own unit and heads on the lexeme (rule 46).

Presentative dummy 'there' joins the finite verb's unit (rule 17). The second colon's 'cometh' realizes the same written verb, gapped in the Hebrew, so both occurrences are this verb's one discontinuous unit under rule 34's second-realization sentence and rule 25; the ASV italic corroborates either reading and decides nothing (rule 7). Marking the second 'cometh' added under rule 34's supplied-lexical-verb sentence was the competing reading, but the Hebrew writes this verb in the coordination.
Waw takes the connective written for it (rule 14).

review_notes: The italic 'cometh' of the second colon is treated as the second realization of the written בָּא rather than as a supplied lexical verb, since the Hebrew writes that verb in the coordination (rule 34).
